Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Great to see how Stratos is using embeddings for content similarity and ad-matching. Per our call, I wanted to capture the technical asks so your engineers have something actionable while we scope the pilot.

Quick recap (from our notes):
- Current vendor: VectraAI (embedding dim: 1536, stored in Pinecone)
- Primary goals: reduce unit cost, improve recall for short queries, and support a reranker stage for ad scoring
- Pilot scope: 1M user-facing docs, offline reranker test, live A/B on 10% traffic

Immediate technical questions we flagged you asked us to confirm:
1) Vector dimension options and cost tradeoffs
2) Batching/throughput expectations for your ingestion (10k docs/day peak)
3) Normalization recommendations (unit normalization vs per-collection avg)
4) How auth and SDK setup will work for private staging vs production
5) Routing and fallback: routing by latency vs cost (how Redwood could fail over to a cheaper quantized model)
6) Structured output and tool-calling support for the reranker + downstream scoring (we suggested deterministic JSON output)

Attachments: I attached a high-level architecture diagram and the pilot MAP (spreadsheet) for dates/owners.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Karthik: technical writeup on vector dim / normalization / batching (deliver EOD 10/14)
- Marissa: pilot MAP with proposed cutover dates and success criteria (deliver 10/15)
- Stratos: confirm sample export from Vectra (format: id, embedding_base64 or floats, metadata) and preferred test dates

If that looks right, please confirm and I’ll book a technical sync with your data infra folks.

Hi Sara — short technical responses to your bullets plus recommendations for the pilot. Ping me if you want a call to dig deeper.

1) Vector dimension options and tradeoffs- We typically recommend evaluating 3 tiers: 768, 1024, 1536. 768 reduces storage/cost ~2x vs 1536, but can lose nuance on short queries; 1024 is often a good middle ground for ad-text. For the pilot: sample 10k queries and compute cosine recall at K=20 across dims to pick the sweet spot.

2) Export format and ingestion- Floats are fine; we can also accept base64. If you export CSV of floats, include header: id,embedding_0..embedding_n,metadata_json so ingestion maps easily. Redwood SDK has an ingestion helper that reads CSVs and streams in batched writes.

3) Batching and throughput- For your peak 10k docs/day the default continuous batching (we call it adaptive batching) will ingest comfortably via a 256-doc minibatch and finish within minutes for typical GPU-backed encoding. For exports to Redwood embeddings store we recommend 512-doc batches for throughput; choose smaller batches if you need stricter ordering or per-doc latency.

4) Normalization- For cross-collection search we recommend per-vector L2 normalization at indexing time (unit length) plus storing collection_mean as metadata to support collection-aware rescoring. If you currently normalize by collection mean, we can accept that during migration but recommend re-normalizing to unit vectors in the pilot to observe recall differences.

5) Auth and SDK setup (staging vs prod)- Options: API keys scoped to projects (fastest), or mTLS with short-lived tokens for private deployments. For your staging environment we suggest scoped API keys tied to a service account; for production we can provision customer-managed service accounts (OAuth2 + role-based). The Redwood SDK supports both flows; we’ll provide a sample service-account manifest and a quickstart repo for Stratos infra.

6) Routing and fallback- We support policy-based routing: route by latency SLO (priority to nearest region) or by cost (fall back to a quantized model during heavy load). For your pilot, enable a two-tier policy: primary (fp16 1024) in us-east, fallback (int8 768) with deterministic response sealing for reranker.

7) Structured output & tool calling for reranker- You can instruct Redwood’s response schema to emit JSON with explicit fields. Example shape for reranker call: {"candidates": [{"id": "doc_123", "embedding_score": 0.82}], "top_k": 5}. We also support pre-specified validators so the reranker only receives well-formed JSON.

Migration playbook (short):
- Phase 0: sample export (Stratos provides 50k vectors in CSV).
- Phase 1: pilot ingest and compare recall across dims (10/20–10/30).
- Phase 2: offline reranker tuning and perf testing (11/1–11/8).
- Phase 3: 10% live A/B, metric collection (11/9–11/13).

I attached a short checklist to the MAP (Marissa will drop it into the spreadsheet). Happy to join your infra sync.

Cheers,
